title: September 2026
note: Directing agents instead of just writing code.

entries.title: An L8 Principal's Agentic Engineering Workflow
entries.description: Kun Chen (ex-Meta L8) ships 40+ well-tested PRs a week by directing a fleet of agents like an engineering manager. As the senior-most dev on my project, this reframed how I think about scaling myself instead of my keystrokes.

entries.title: Forget Everything You Know About Writing Code in 2026
entries.description: A reality-check on how the day-to-day of engineering is shifting from typing code to specifying, orchestrating and reviewing it. Lines up with what I'm already feeling on our own stack.

entries.title: Building Effective Agents
entries.description: Anthropic's breakdown of when to reach for workflows vs. agents, and the composable patterns behind each. My reference point for the CrewAI / multi-agent work at Astro.

title: August 2026
note: The business and systems behind the tech.

entries.title: How America's 4,488 Banks Work
entries.description: A PolyMatter case study on why the US still runs thousands of tiny banks. I keep coming back to these systems-thinking breakdowns - they're the closest thing to a design review for the real world.

entries.title: How to 10x Your Value in the A.I. Era — ft. Kunal Shah
entries.description: The CRED founder on leverage when 90% of a startup's code is AI-written. A useful gut-check on where a developer's value actually moves next.

entries.title: Why the Grand Seiko Spring Drive Is the Greatest Watch Movement
entries.description: Off the clock: I fall down analog-watch rabbit holes. The Spring Drive's glide-motion seconds hand is peak engineering - a few hundred hand-finished parts keeping near-perfect time with zero electronics.

title: July 2026
note: Keeping a finger on the tech news cycle.

entries.title: CIA's Secret: How Peter Thiel Built a $200B Weapon
entries.description: A Think School deep-dive on Palantir - how a data-analytics company became critical infrastructure for the state. Equal parts product, politics and power.

entries.title: Fireship: Anthropic leaks Claude's source code
entries.description: Fireship is my 100-second pulse on the tech news cycle - new frameworks, model drops and the occasional roast. This take on an Anthropic slip-up is the format at its best.

entries.title: Theo (t3.gg): Did GPT-6 Break Out During Testing?
entries.description: Theo Browne's opinionated, in-the-weeds takes on AI tooling, web dev and the SDE news cycle. A good counterweight to the hype - I keep him in regular rotation.

entries.title: Use The Index, Luke!
entries.description: A developer's ground-up guide to how SQL indexing really works. This mental model directly fed the 35% storage and query-time wins I made on our PostgreSQL layer.

title: June 2026
note: Range: startups, culture and where value is heading.

entries.title: Y Combinator: Why 80% of Apps Will Disappear — OpenClaw Creator
entries.description: Founder talks and startup teardowns I keep in rotation. Even from the engineering seat, thinking like a builder-of-the-business changes the calls I make on architecture and scope.

entries.title: छत्रपती शिवाजी महाराज आणि मराठा साम्राज्य
entries.description: A Ketan Puri Marathi podcast on Shivaji Maharaj and the Maratha empire. Homegrown history, and quietly a masterclass in leadership, delegation and playing the long game.

entries.title: Neuroscientist's Guide to 10x Your Focus & Memory — ft. Dr Sahar Yousef
entries.description: From Raj Shamani's Figuring Out - a neuroscientist on evidence-based focus and memory. The kind of long-form podcast I lean on to sharpen how I work, lead and mentor, not just what I build.
